landing.title: Votain
landing.hero_desc: Participate in democratic processes with full privacy. Votain uses cryptographic proofs to ensure your vote counts without revealing your identity.

onboarding.what_desc: Vote safely and secretly from any device. No one will ever know what you chose.
onboarding.privacy_desc: World ID signs you in without telling us who you are, and our server keeps nothing. Your voting identity is sealed with your passkey, so only you can open it.
onboarding.coercion_desc: If someone forces you to vote, you can do it again in secret later. Only the last one counts.
onboarding.free_desc: You don't need to pay anything or understand crypto. The organizer handles everything.
onboarding.name_title: How should you appear as organizer?
onboarding.name_desc: This name is shown on every election you create. It is stored with each election when you create it, so renaming yourself later does not change the ones already published.

verify.title: Verify your Identity
verify.description: World ID signs you in anonymously: we never see your name, your face or your documents. It identifies an account rather than a person, so each election sets for itself how strongly a voter must prove they are one human.
verify.mobile_return_hint: After verifying in the app, come back to this tab
verify.qr_desc: Open the World ID app and scan this code to verify your identity.
verify.error_backend: Verification failed on our end. Please try again.
verify.error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
verify.open_desc: We will take you to the World ID app to verify your identity.

voting_type.two_thirds_desc: Approved with at least 2/3 of the votes cast. Works for a yes/no motion or a field of candidates
voting_type.witness_threshold_desc: Yes/No: approved with at least N confirmations

election.witness_rule_other: Approved with at least {{count}} yes votes

how.title: How Votain works
how.subtitle: End-to-end verifiable voting, anonymous and coercion-resistant: built on open standards.
how.step1_desc: World ID gives you an account without revealing who you are. An election that needs one person, one vote also asks for a document check on your own phone, which discloses nothing else.
how.step2_desc: Your vote is encrypted on your device, and a zero-knowledge proof gets it counted without revealing your choice. Each election you join also sees a different identity, so the chain never says which elections you took part in.
how.step3_desc: If coerced, you can vote again later. Only your last vote counts, so your true choice is always safe.
how.step4_desc: Every encrypted ballot and the final tally live on the blockchain. Anyone can recount them without breaking anyone’s anonymity.

results.title: Results
results.check_ok_body: The published counts add up to {{declared}}, and the contract recorded {{voters}} voters. No ballot was invented or dropped.
results.check_bad_body: The published counts add up to {{declared}}, but the contract recorded {{voters}} voters. These should be the same number.
results.check_limit: This needs no key and no trust: anyone can repeat it. It cannot tell whether votes were moved between options, which keeps the total unchanged.

verify_receipt.title: Verify a vote
verify_receipt.subtitle: Enter a reference number or nullifier to confirm a ballot was recorded on-chain.
verify_receipt.hint: A reference number is shown after voting, and again in the voter history.
verify_receipt.not_found_desc: No matching vote was found. Check your reference number and try again.
verify_receipt.choice_never_shown: The chain records that a ballot was cast and when, never what it said. Nobody can read a choice from a receipt, including us.
verify_receipt.unlock_hint: This browser knows of no ballot yet. If you voted from another device, one passkey tap will find those and remember them here.

reverify.title: Recover your voting identity
reverify.desc: Lost your recovery phrase and every passkey that held it? Verify with World ID again to start over with a new phrase.
reverify.reason1: I have lost my twelve-word recovery phrase
reverify.reason2: And every passkey that held a copy of it: a lost device, a deleted passkey, cleared browser data
reverify.reason3: Typing the phrase would get everything back at no cost, and that is not open to me
reverify.recovered_desc: This device now holds your voting identity. You can vote in elections you had not joined yet.
reverify.cost_elections: You will not be able to rejoin elections you had already enrolled in, even if you never voted in them.
reverify.cost_receipts: Your previous vote receipts stop being retrievable, though those ballots stay valid and counted.
reverify.one_identity_note: Your World ID can only have one active voting identity, and every identity it has ever had stays bound to it. That is why the old elections stay closed.

org_auth.title: Organizer Access
org_auth.subtitle: Sign in with the wallet that will own your elections
org_auth.wallet_desc: Connect the Polygon wallet you want to organize with. It will own the elections you create and sign every change to them.
org_auth.wallet_desc_back: Connect the wallet you organized with before. Your elections are found by its address.
org_auth.wallet_is_identity: Votain has no accounts. Your wallet is your identity here, and the key that opens your results is derived from it.
org_auth.no_wallet_desc: Install MetaMask (or another EVM wallet) to sign as an organizer.
org_auth.subtitle_back: Sign in with the wallet you organized with
org_auth.no_wallet_mobile: A wallet on a phone lives inside its own app and cannot be reached from this page. Organizing is meant for a computer with the wallet extension.

create.blank_vote_note: A blank vote option is always included automatically.
create.quorum_hint: Minimum votes required before results are revealed.
create.deposit_hint: Optional. Reserved for THIS election and cannot be withdrawn until it ends, which is what lets voters see that their ballot is paid for. You can add more later.
create.immutability_warning: Once deployed, the election parameters cannot be changed. Review everything carefully.
create.deploy_confirm_desc: This deploys a smart contract and adds {{amount}} {{currency}} from your wallet to your shared gas tank.
create.witness_threshold_hint: Minimum Yes votes needed to approve
create.yes_no_note: This voting type always uses a fixed Yes / No ballot.
create.leave_confirm_desc: Your changes will be lost if you leave this page.
create.separate_enrollment_desc: Set your own registration dates, with a deadline that can fall before voting opens.
create.enrollment_until_vote_start: Registration is open from deployment until voting starts.
create.yes_no_hint: There is nothing to configure here: the options are set by the voting rule you chose. Voters will pick one of them.
create.short_enrollment_warning: Voting starts in under a day, and enrolment closes when it opens. Voters who do not join in time cannot vote at all. Consider a later start, or a separate enrolment window.
create.eligibility_enable_desc: Voters prove an age or a nationality from the chip in their identity document before they can join. They will need the Self app and an NFC phone.
create.eligibility_unavailable: The verification service is not reachable, so this election could not be created with restrictions. Leave the switch off, or try again later.
create.min_age_hint: Leave empty for no age rule. The date of birth is never revealed, only whether it clears this threshold.
create.nationality_reveal_note: Allowing only certain countries makes voters disclose their nationality, because the proof system can only express exclusions. Blocking countries does not: it answers yes or no without naming the country.
create.country_picker_hint: Search and pick countries. Up to {{max}}.
create.personhood_desc: How sure this election needs to be that two enrolments are two different people.
create.personhood_device_desc: One account, one vote. Quick, and worth what an account is worth: a voter with a second account can enrol twice.
create.personhood_document_desc: The voter proves a passport or national ID card on their own phone. Nothing about the document is revealed, and a second enrolment behind the same one is refused.
create.personhood_orb: An identity document and a World ID Orb
create.personhood_orb_desc: The strongest bar, and the narrowest: Orb verification is unavailable in countries where the Orbs were withdrawn, and those voters will not be able to enrol.
create.fixed_schedule_desc: Give up the power to close enrolment or voting early. Voters see this on the election, and it cannot be undone. Cancelling the election is still possible.
create.no_cancel_desc: Give up the power to cancel this election. It will run to its end whatever the turnout looks like, and voters see this on the election.
create.no_way_back: With both given up, this election runs exactly as published: a mistake in these dates cannot be corrected or called off.

profile.nullifier_hint: Your anonymous identifier on Votain. It stops anyone registering twice, and reveals nothing about you or your vote.
profile.wallet_note: Your organizer identity. It owns your elections, signs every change to them, and derives the key that opens their results.

profile.also_voter_title: Do you want to vote too?
profile.also_voter_desc: Sign in as a voter with World ID to enrol in elections and cast a ballot. Your organizer session stays exactly as it is, and the header lets you switch between the two.

profile.sign_out_organizer_desc: The wallet and display name remembered on this device are cleared. The keys that decrypt your elections stay, so published results remain readable. Your voter session is untouched.
profile.sign_out_both_desc: Both sessions end and you return to the home screen.
profile.sign_out_voter_only_desc: Your voting identity, the twelve words if they were stored here, and the votes recorded on this device are deleted from this browser. To come back you will need a linked passkey or your recovery phrase.
profile.sign_out_organizer_only_desc: The wallet and display name this device remembered are cleared. The keys that decrypt your elections stay, so published results remain readable.
profile.cancel_signup_desc: Nothing has been registered yet: your identity is not on the registry. The twelve words generated on this device are discarded and your World ID session ends. You can start again whenever you like.
profile.reverify_hint: Lost a device, or had one stolen? Rotating your identity revokes the old one, and with it every election you had already joined.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.what_1: Votain is a Bachelor's thesis project: an end-to-end verifiable, anonymous voting application built on the Polygon Amoy test network. It is a research prototype, not a commercial service.
terms.what_2: It runs on a TEST network. The tokens it uses have no monetary value and the network offers no guarantee of persistence: test networks are reset or discontinued from time to time, and any election held here can disappear with them.
terms.binding_title: Elections held here are not legally binding
terms.binding_1: Nothing you organise or vote in through Votain has legal effect. It does not constitute an official election, referendum, corporate resolution, notarial act or any other legally recognised process.
terms.binding_2: Do not use Votain for any vote whose outcome must stand up legally, or where a wrong or lost result would cause real harm.
terms.identity_1: Voting requires a World ID account and a twelve-word recovery phrase that Votain generates on your device. World ID identifies the account rather than the person; an election that requires one person, one vote asks for a document check as well. Your phrase is never sent to us and cannot be recovered by us.
terms.identity_2: Whoever has the phrase can restore the identity on any device, with no passkey and no help from us. If you lose the phrase and every passkey holding it, verifying with World ID again lets you start over. Starting over is deliberately limited: you can join elections you had not yet enrolled in, but never re-enter one you had, because the system cannot tell whether you already voted there without breaking the anonymity of the ballot.
terms.organizer_1: You are responsible for what you put on chain. Election names, descriptions and candidate lists are stored publicly and permanently, and cannot be edited or deleted once published. Do not put personal data of third parties in them.
terms.organizer_2: You fund a single gas tank that pays transaction fees for the voters of ALL your elections. If it empties, voting stops across every one of them until you top it up.
terms.warranty_1: Votain is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. It has not been independently audited. It may contain defects that affect the correctness, availability or privacy of a vote.
terms.warranty_2: To the maximum extent permitted by law, the author accepts no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use.
terms.licence_1: Votain is released under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. The full source code is public, which is what allows anyone to check that the software does what this page says it does.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.summary_1: We never learn your name, your face or your biometrics. We do not know how you voted, and neither does the organizer, because ballots are encrypted before they leave your device and only the final total is ever decrypted.
privacy.summary_2: This page describes what actually happens in the software rather than what is merely permitted, including the places where the design does not protect you.
privacy.worldid_1: When you verify, World ID sends us a proof and a nullifier: a number derived from you and from this application. It is the same every time you return, which is how one account is stopped from enrolling twice in the same election, and it is different for every application you use World ID with. It does not prove you are one person: an election that needs that asks for a document check as well, which yields a second number, scoped to that election alone.
privacy.worldid_2: We receive no other personal data from World ID. Your biometrics never leave your own device and are never transmitted to us.
privacy.identity_1: Your voting secret is a phrase generated on your device and shown to you once, so you can keep it. Where a passkey can hold it, a sealed copy is stored for each passkey you register, so you can vote from several devices without typing anything. Those copies are written to the blockchain rather than to our server, so losing us cannot lock you out, and what opens them never leaves your authenticator. We never see the phrase and cannot recover it for you.
privacy.identity_2: This is not a formality. If we could decrypt it, we could compute the identifier your ballot carries and match every vote to the person who cast it. The encryption is what makes that impossible for us, not just forbidden.
privacy.ballot_1: Your choice is encrypted in your browser before it is submitted, using a key held by the organizer. Ballots are added together while still encrypted, and only the sum is decrypted, so no individual vote is ever revealed to anyone, including the organizer.
privacy.ballot_2: You may vote again as many times as you like; only your last ballot counts. Earlier ones remain stored but are indistinguishable from it, which is what allows you to quietly replace a vote you were pressured into casting.
privacy.onchain_title: What is public on the blockchain
privacy.onchain_1: Public and permanent: which elections exist, that a given identity is registered on the platform, that somebody the platform verified enrolled in each election, the encrypted ballots with their published totals, and the sealed copies of each voting identity, one per registered passkey. What enrols is a commitment derived for that election alone, so the chain does not say which elections any one person joined. Anyone can read all of it. The sealed copies are ciphertext and open only with the passkey that made them, but their existence and their number are visible.
privacy.onchain_2: Not public: the link between an enrolled identity and any particular ballot, nor the link between the same person's enrolments in different elections. Breaking the first is what the zero-knowledge proof exists for, and it is why every vote is submitted through one shared contract rather than from an address of your own. The second is why what enrols is derived for each election instead of being reused.
privacy.limits_title: What this does not protect you from
privacy.limits_1: When you submit a vote, the request reaches our server from your network connection, so its origin is visible to us in the same way it is to any website you use. We do not use it to identify voters, but the design does not prevent us from doing so, and you should know that before relying on the anonymity of your ballot.
privacy.limits_2: The issuer is also a point of trust: it verifies World ID proofs, registers voters and signs each enrolment, which makes it the one party able to tell which elections you joined. A dishonest issuer could add voters who do not exist. It could not read your ballot or alter the count, but you are relying on it being honest about who is allowed to vote and discreet about where you voted.
privacy.retention_1: We keep nothing on our own servers: your session lives in a cookie in your browser, and everything durable is on the blockchain. Removing a passkey removes its sealed copy from the chain; removing the last one is refused, because it would leave your identity permanently unusable.
privacy.retention_2: Anything already written to the blockchain cannot be deleted by us or by anyone else. That is inherent to a public ledger and is the same property that lets you verify your vote was counted.

recovery.title: Write these twelve words down
recovery.intro: They rebuild your anonymous voting identity on any device. You can look them up again from your profile while you still have access here, and nobody can recover them for you once you do not.
recovery.warning: Anyone with these words can vote as you. Keep them somewhere only you can reach, and never type them into anything that is not Votain.
recovery.show_desc: The twelve words your voting identity is built from. Anyone holding them can vote as you, so they stay hidden until you ask for them.
recovery.unavailable: This device cannot show your phrase
recovery.unavailable_help: It is held by a passkey this browser could not reach. Try a device you can vote from, or type the words in on the recovery page.
recovery.copy_failed: Your browser did not allow copying. Write the words down instead.
recovery.unregistered_title: Your passkey works, but it is not registered yet
recovery.unregistered_desc: It was created and your phrase was encrypted with it, but the copy could not be saved to the chain. Your twelve words stay on this device meanwhile, so keep them safe. You can retry the registration from your profile.

recover.title: Restore your identity
recover.intro: Type the twelve words you were given when you first verified. They rebuild the same identity, with the elections you already joined.
recover.unknown_words: Not words from the list: {{words}}. Check for a typo.
recover.not_registered: Those words rebuild no known identity
recover.not_registered_desc: The phrase is well formed, so the words are on the list, but the identity it rebuilds has never been registered. Check for a word in the wrong place.
recover.help: The words are all lowercase and the order matters. Spaces and capitals do not.
recover.kept_on_device: Identity restored, phrase kept on this device
recover.kept_on_device_desc: Without a passkey your twelve words stay on this browser unencrypted. You can link one later from your profile.
recover.have_passkey: I do have my passkey after all

identity_step.has_passkey_desc: You already have an identity saved. Continue and this device will ask for your passkey to open it: the usual fingerprint or PIN.
identity_step.phrase_only_desc: No passkey was ever linked to this identity, so your twelve words are the only way to get it back. If you do not have them, you can start over from there.
identity_step.new_desc: This is the anonymous identity you will vote with, kept apart from your World ID. We will show you twelve words to recover it and, if this device can, protect it with a passkey.
identity_step.unknown_desc: We could not check the state of your identity. You can try anyway.
identity_step.no_passkey_access: I cannot use my passkey right now

new_identity.confirm_title: Have you saved your phrase somewhere safe?
new_identity.confirm_desc: Nobody can recover it for you. If you lose these twelve words and have no passkey linked, you lose your vote.
new_identity.passkey_desc: It encrypts your twelve words with your fingerprint, face or a device PIN, and keeps that encrypted copy off this machine. You never have to type them, and they stop sitting here in the clear.
new_identity.no_prf_title: This passkey cannot hold your phrase
new_identity.no_prf_desc: It was created, but your device will not let it decrypt, so it could not bring you back. Try another one: your phone's, scanned as a QR code, usually works. You can also link one later from your profile.
new_identity.skip_desc: Your twelve words stay on this device unencrypted until you link one.
new_identity.skip_confirm_desc: Your twelve words will stay stored on this device unencrypted, and they will be your only way back. You can link a passkey later from your profile, whenever you like.

schedule.fixed_desc: The organizer gave up the power to move any deadline when this election was created. The published dates are the dates it will run to.
schedule.fixed_desc_own: You gave up the power to move any deadline when you created this election. The published dates are the dates it will run to.
schedule.movable_desc: The organizer can bring any of this election’s dates forward or cut a period short. They can also see how many people have enrolled and voted while deciding.
schedule.movable_desc_own: You can bring any of this election’s dates forward or cut a period short, and while you decide you can see how many people have enrolled and voted.
schedule.no_cancel_desc: The organizer gave up the power to cancel this election when it was created. It will run to its end whatever the turnout looks like.
schedule.no_cancel_desc_own: You gave up the power to cancel this election when you created it. It will run to its end whatever the turnout looks like.
schedule.can_cancel: The organizer can call it off
schedule.can_cancel_desc: The organizer may cancel this election while it runs. No result is published if they do.
schedule.can_cancel_desc_own: You can cancel this election while it runs. No result is published if you do.

funding.unfunded_title: This election cannot pay for ballots right now
funding.unfunded_body: Every ballot here is paid for by the organizer, so that voting needs no wallet. Their balance for this election is empty. Nothing is wrong with your identity: ask the organizer to top it up and come back.
funding.short: About {{votes}} more ballots are funded, and {{voters}} people who enrolled have not voted yet.
funding.reserved_votes: About {{votes}} ballots are reserved for this election.

timeline.title: Schedule
timeline.abandoned: This election was stopped, so this schedule was not followed to the end.

sort.partial_notice: ordered over what has been read so far
